attributes.name: aga_calculation_method
attributes.description: Standard calculation method used for gas flow measurement. AGA-3 for orifice meters, AGA-7 for turbine meters, AGA-9 for ultrasonic meters, AGA-11 for coriolis meters.
attributes.references: AGA Report No. 3 / AGA Report No. 7 / AGA Report No. 9

attributes.name: allocation_method
attributes.description: Method used to allocate measured gas volumes among multiple wells or owners. Proportional allocation uses well test data; priority allocation follows contractual hierarchy; test-based uses recent well tests.

attributes.name: atmospheric_pressure_psia
attributes.business_glossary_term: Atmospheric Pressure (PSIA - Pounds per Square Inch Absolute)
attributes.description: Atmospheric pressure at the meter location in pounds per square inch absolute. Used to convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure for flow calculations.

attributes.name: base_pressure_psia
attributes.business_glossary_term: Base Pressure (PSIA - Pounds per Square Inch Absolute)
attributes.description: Standard reference pressure for volume correction, typically 14.73 psia. Contractually defined base condition for custody transfer calculations.

attributes.name: base_temperature_f
attributes.description: Standard reference temperature for volume correction, typically 60°F. Contractually defined base condition for custody transfer calculations.

attributes.name: co2_content_mol_percent
attributes.description: Mole percentage of carbon dioxide in the gas stream. Important for heating value calculation, pipeline quality specifications, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reporting.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14.1 - Collecting and Handling of Natural Gas Samples

attributes.name: compressibility_factor
attributes.description: Dimensionless factor accounting for deviation of real gas behavior from ideal gas law. Calculated using AGA-8 or other methods based on gas composition, temperature, and pressure.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14.2 / AGA Report No. 8

attributes.name: corrected_volume_mcf
attributes.description: Gas volume corrected to standard base conditions (typically 14.73 psia and 60°F) in thousand cubic feet. This is the volume used for custody transfer and sales calculations.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the gas measurement record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: differential_pressure_inches_h2o
attributes.description: Pressure drop across the orifice plate in inches of water column. Used in AGA-3 orifice meter flow calculations. Higher differential indicates higher flow rate.

attributes.name: energy_content_mmbtu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Energy Content (MMBtu - Million British Thermal Units)
attributes.description: Total energy content of the measured gas volume in million British thermal units. Calculated by multiplying corrected volume by heating value. Used for gas sales invoicing and pipeline tariff billing.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14.5 - Calculation of Gross Heating Value

attributes.name: estimation_method
attributes.description: Description of the method used to estimate gas volume when meter data is unavailable or invalid. Examples include historical average, adjacent meter correlation, or well test extrapolation.

attributes.name: flowing_pressure_psig
attributes.business_glossary_term: Flowing Pressure (PSIG - Pounds per Square Inch Gauge)
attributes.description: Pressure of the gas at the meter during measurement in pounds per square inch gauge. Used to correct volume to standard base conditions per AGA calculation methods.

attributes.name: flowing_temperature_f
attributes.description: Temperature of the gas at the meter during measurement in degrees Fahrenheit. Used to correct volume to standard base conditions per AGA calculation methods.

attributes.name: h2s_content_mol_percent
attributes.description: Mole percentage of hydrogen sulfide in the gas stream. Critical for safety, corrosion management, and pipeline quality specifications. Sour gas typically contains >4 ppm H2S.

attributes.name: heating_value_btu_per_scf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Heating Value (BTU per SCF - British Thermal Units per Standard Cubic Foot)
attributes.description: Gross heating value of the gas in BTU per standard cubic foot. Determined by gas chromatograph analysis or calculated from gas composition. Critical for energy-based sales contracts.

attributes.name: measurement_date
attributes.description: Calendar date of the gas measurement for daily production reporting and allocation. Used for aggregating daily production volumes (MCFD/MMCFD).

attributes.name: measurement_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the gas measurement period ended. Defines the end of the custody transfer or allocation interval.

attributes.name: measurement_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the gas measurement transaction. Externally-known reference number used in custody transfer documentation and regulatory filings.

attributes.name: measurement_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the gas measurement period began. Defines the beginning of the custody transfer or allocation interval.

attributes.name: measurement_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the gas measurement record. Validated measurements have passed quality checks; approved measurements are ready for billing; final measurements are locked for regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: measurement_type
attributes.description: Classification of the gas measurement purpose. Custody transfer measurements are used for sales and royalty calculations; allocation measurements distribute production among wells or facilities; check measurements validate meter accuracy.

attributes.name: meter_factor
attributes.description: Correction factor applied to raw meter readings to account for meter calibration and performance characteristics. Determined through meter proving or calibration. Typically near 1.0000.

attributes.name: meter_tube_diameter_inches
attributes.description: Internal diameter of the meter tube in inches. Used in AGA-3 flow calculations to determine beta ratio (orifice diameter / pipe diameter).

attributes.name: methane_content_mol_percent
attributes.description: Mole percentage of methane in the gas stream. Primary component of natural gas, typically 70-90%. Used in heating value calculation and compressibility factor determination.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the gas measurement record was last modified. Audit trail field for tracking corrections and adjustments.

attributes.name: nitrogen_content_mol_percent
attributes.description: Mole percentage of nitrogen in the gas stream. Affects heating value and compressibility. High nitrogen content reduces energy content and may require contract adjustments.

attributes.name: orifice_plate_size_inches
attributes.description: Diameter of the orifice plate opening in inches. Used in AGA-3 flow calculations. Must be smaller than pipe diameter to create differential pressure.

attributes.name: quality_flag
attributes.description: Data quality indicator for the measurement. Suspect measurements require review; estimated measurements use historical averages; failed measurements indicate meter malfunction.

attributes.name: raw_volume_mcf
attributes.description: Uncorrected gas volume measured at the meter in thousand cubic feet. This is the raw meter reading before applying temperature, pressure, and compressibility corrections.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14.3 - Natural Gas Fluids Measurement

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text notes regarding measurement conditions, anomalies, or adjustments. Used to document meter issues, estimation rationale, or custody transfer disputes.

attributes.name: specific_gravity
attributes.description: Ratio of the density of the gas to the density of air at standard conditions. Used in flow calculation algorithms and compressibility factor determination. Typical range 0.55 to 0.75 for natural gas.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14.2 - Orifice Metering of Natural Gas

attributes.name: validation_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the measurement was validated and approved for billing and regulatory reporting. Marks transition from draft to validated status.

attributes.name: combustion_efficiency_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of gas that is fully combusted in the flare. Typically 98% or higher for properly designed flares. Used for emissions calculations.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, observations, or context about the flaring event not captured in structured fields.

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Indicator of the quality and reliability of the flare volume data. Verified indicates direct measurement and validation, estimated indicates calculated values.

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Source system or method from which the flare record data was captured. Examples include OSIsoft PI System, SCADA, manual entry, or third-party measurement.

attributes.name: economic_loss_usd
attributes.description: Estimated revenue loss from flaring the gas instead of selling it, calculated using current gas price and flared volume. Expressed in US dollars.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 1200 - Disclosure of Reserves

attributes.name: flare_date
attributes.description: Calendar date of the flaring event for daily aggregation and reporting. Format yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: flare_duration_hours
attributes.description: Total duration of the flaring event in hours. Calculated from start and end timestamps.
attributes.references: API Standard 521 - Pressure-relieving and Depressuring Systems

attributes.name: flare_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the flaring event ended. Null for ongoing flaring events. Recorded in format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 - Mandatory Greenhouse Gas Reporting

attributes.name: flare_event_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the flaring event. Used for tracking and regulatory reporting purposes.
attributes.references: BSEE NTL 2016-N01 - Flaring or Venting of Gas

attributes.name: flare_reason_code
attributes.description: Standardized code indicating the reason for the flaring event. Used for root cause analysis and regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: planned_maintenance|unplanned_maintenance|startup|shutdown|emergency_relief|process_upset|equipment_failure|gas_quality|no_sales_outlet|well_testing|production_optimization|regulatory_compliance — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: BSEE NTL 2016-N01 - Flaring or Venting of Gas; API Recommended Practice 521

attributes.name: flare_reason_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the reason for flaring, including specific equipment, process conditions, or operational circumstances.

attributes.name: flare_start_timestamp

attributes.name: flare_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the flare record. Active indicates ongoing flaring, completed indicates event has ended and data is finalized.

attributes.name: flare_type
attributes.description: Classification of the flaring event by operational pattern. Continuous flaring is ongoing, intermittent is periodic, emergency is unplanned safety relief, routine is planned operational flaring.
attributes.references: API Standard 521 - Pressure-relieving and Depressuring Systems

attributes.name: flare_volume_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Flare Volume (BOE - Barrel of Oil Equivalent)
attributes.description: Flared gas volume converted to barrel of oil equivalent using standard conversion factor (typically 6 MCF = 1 BOE). Used for economic impact analysis.
attributes.references: SEC Regulation S-K Item 1200 - Disclosure of Reserves

attributes.name: flare_volume_mcf
attributes.description: Total volume of gas flared during the event measured in thousand cubic feet. Alternative unit for internal reporting.

attributes.name: flare_volume_mscf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Flare Volume (MSCF - Thousand Standard Cubic Feet)
attributes.description: Total volume of gas flared during the event measured in thousand standard cubic feet. Primary metric for regulatory reporting and emissions calculations.
attributes.references: BSEE NTL 2016-N01 - Flaring or Venting of Gas; EPA 40 CFR Part 98 Subpart W

attributes.name: gas_composition_co2_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of carbon dioxide in the flared gas stream. Critical for emissions reporting.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 - Mandatory Greenhouse Gas Reporting

attributes.name: gas_composition_ethane_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of ethane (C2H6) in the flared gas stream.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14.1 - Natural Gas Fluids Measurement

attributes.name: gas_composition_h2s_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gas Composition Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) Content (PPM - Parts Per Million)
attributes.description: Concentration of hydrogen sulfide in the flared gas measured in parts per million. Critical for safety and environmental compliance.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1000 - Air Contaminants; API RP 55 - Safe Practices for Gas and Oil Well Servicing

attributes.name: gas_composition_methane_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of methane (CH4) in the flared gas stream. Used for greenhouse gas emissions calculations.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 Subpart W - Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems

attributes.name: gas_composition_propane_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of propane (C3H8) in the flared gas stream.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14.1 - Natural Gas Fluids Measurement

attributes.name: gas_price_usd_per_mcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Gas Price (USD per MCF - United States Dollars per Thousand Cubic Feet)
attributes.description: Market price of natural gas at the time of flaring, used for economic loss calculations. Expressed in US dollars per thousand cubic feet.
attributes.references: NYMEX Henry Hub Natural Gas Futures; Internal Pricing Deck

attributes.name: ghg_emissions_co2e_tonnes
attributes.description: Total greenhouse gas emissions from the flaring event expressed as carbon dioxide equivalent in metric tonnes. Calculated using EPA or IPCC methodologies.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 - Mandatory Greenhouse Gas Reporting; IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories

attributes.name: heating_value_btu_per_scf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Heating Value (BTU per SCF - British Thermal Units per Standard Cubic Foot)
attributes.description: Energy content of the flared gas measured in British Thermal Units per standard cubic foot. Used for economic loss calculations.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14.5 - Calculation of Gross Heating Value, Relative Density, Compressibility and Theoretical Hydrocarbon Liquid Content

attributes.name: measurement_method
attributes.description: Method used to measure or estimate the volume of flared gas. Direct measurement is preferred for regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14 - Natural Gas Fluids Measurement; EPA 40 CFR Part 98

attributes.name: permit_number
attributes.description: Permit or authorization number issued by regulatory agency allowing the flaring activity. Required for planned flaring in many jurisdictions.
attributes.references: BSEE 30 CFR 250 - Oil and Gas and Sulphur Operations in the Outer Continental Shelf

attributes.name: record_created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this flare record was first created in the system. Format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: record_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this flare record was last modified. Format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: regulatory_reportable_flag

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_date
attributes.description: Date when the flaring event was reported to the regulatory agency. Format yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: specific_gravity
attributes.description: Specific gravity of the flared gas relative to air. Used for volume and emissions calculations.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14.3 - Orifice Metering of Natural Gas

attributes.name: vented_volume_mscf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Vented Volume (MSCF - Thousand Standard Cubic Feet)
attributes.description: Volume of gas vented (released without combustion) during the event in thousand standard cubic feet. Tracked separately from flared volume for environmental compliance.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 98 Subpart W - Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems; BSEE NTL 2016-N01

attributes.description: Number of alkylation units installed at the refinery. Alkylation units combine light olefins with isobutane to produce high-octane gasoline blending components.

attributes.name: api_facility_number
attributes.description: Facility registration number assigned by the American Petroleum Institute for industry reporting and standards compliance.

attributes.name: cdu_unit_count
attributes.description: Number of crude distillation units installed at the refinery. CDUs perform the primary separation of crude oil into fractions based on boiling point ranges.

attributes.name: city
attributes.description: City or municipality where the refinery facility is located.

attributes.name: coker_unit_count
attributes.description: Number of delayed coking units installed at the refinery. Cokers thermally crack heavy residual oils into lighter products and petroleum coke.

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when the refinery facility was officially commissioned and began commercial operations. Used for asset lifecycle tracking and depreciation calculations.

attributes.name: country_code

attributes.name: dcs_system_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the refinery distributed control system. Links the refinery master record to real-time process control and SCADA data.

attributes.name: facility_type
attributes.description: Classification of the refinery based on its processing complexity and unit configuration. Integrated refineries have full conversion capabilities, hydroskimming refineries have basic distillation, conversion refineries focus on upgrading heavy crude, and specialty refineries produce niche products.

attributes.name: fcc_unit_count
attributes.description: Number of fluid catalytic cracking units installed at the refinery. FCC units convert heavy gas oils into lighter, more valuable products such as gasoline and light olefins using catalytic cracking.

attributes.name: hds_unit_count
attributes.description: Number of hydrodesulfurization units installed at the refinery. HDS units remove sulfur from petroleum fractions to meet environmental regulations and product specifications.

attributes.name: hydrocracker_unit_count
attributes.description: Number of hydrocracking units installed at the refinery. Hydrocrackers use hydrogen and catalysts to break down heavy oils into lighter, higher-value products.

attributes.name: is_tier_3_compliant
attributes.description: Indicates whether the refinery meets EPA Tier 3 gasoline sulfur standards requiring sulfur content below 10 ppm. Critical for regulatory compliance and product marketing.
attributes.references: EPA Tier 3 Vehicle Emission and Fuel Standards

attributes.name: is_ulsd_capable
attributes.description: Indicates whether the refinery has the capability to produce ultra-low sulfur diesel with sulfur content below 15 ppm as required by EPA regulations.

attributes.name: last_turnaround_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent major turnaround or planned maintenance shutdown. Turnarounds are comprehensive maintenance events that occur every 3-5 years.

attributes.name: latitude
attributes.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the refinery facility in decimal degrees. Used for mapping, logistics planning, and regulatory jurisdiction determination.

attributes.name: longitude
attributes.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the refinery facility in decimal degrees. Used for mapping, logistics planning, and regulatory jurisdiction determination.

attributes.name: nameplate_capacity_bopd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Nameplate Capacity in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
attributes.description: Maximum designed crude oil processing capacity of the refinery measured in barrels of oil per day under optimal operating conditions. This is the theoretical maximum throughput as designed by the engineering team.

attributes.name: nelson_complexity_index
attributes.description: Industry-standard measure of refinery complexity based on the relative cost and sophistication of processing units. Higher values indicate more complex refineries with greater conversion and upgrading capabilities. Typical range is 1.0 to 15.0.
attributes.references: Oil & Gas Journal - Nelson Complexity Index Methodology

attributes.name: next_turnaround_date
attributes.description: Planned date for the next major turnaround or maintenance shutdown. Used for maintenance planning, budgeting, and production forecasting.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the refinery facility. Operating indicates normal production, turnaround indicates scheduled maintenance shutdown, idle indicates temporary suspension, decommissioned indicates permanent closure, and under construction indicates facility is being built.

attributes.name: ownership_type
attributes.description: Legal ownership structure of the refinery facility. Wholly owned indicates 100% ownership by Oil Gas, joint venture indicates shared ownership with partners, leased indicates the facility is leased from another party, and operated indicates Oil Gas operates but does not own the facility.

attributes.name: pi_system_site_name
attributes.description: Site name in the OSIsoft PI System historian that stores real-time and historical process data for this refinery. Used for data integration and analytics.

attributes.name: postal_code
attributes.description: Postal or ZIP code for the refinery facility location.

attributes.name: primary_feedstock_type
attributes.description: Predominant type of crude oil feedstock processed by the refinery. Light sweet crude has low sulfur and high API gravity, medium sour has moderate sulfur, heavy sour has high sulfur and low API gravity, synthetic is from oil sands, and blended is a mix of multiple crude types.
attributes.references: API Gravity and Sulfur Content Classification

attributes.name: refinery_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code used to identify the refinery in operational systems, reports, and inter-facility communications. Typically 3-10 characters.

attributes.name: refinery_name
attributes.description: Official business name of the refinery facility as registered with regulatory authorities and used in operational reporting.

attributes.name: reformer_unit_count
attributes.description: Number of catalytic reforming units installed at the refinery. Reformers convert low-octane naphtha into high-octane gasoline blending components and produce hydrogen as a byproduct.

attributes.name: renewable_diesel_capacity_bopd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Renewable Diesel Capacity in Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
attributes.description: Maximum production capacity for renewable diesel from bio-based feedstocks measured in barrels per day. Zero if the refinery does not have renewable diesel capability.

attributes.name: state_province
attributes.description: State, province, or primary administrative division where the refinery facility is located. Used for regulatory jurisdiction and tax purposes.

attributes.name: street_address
attributes.description: Physical street address of the refinery facility including street number, street name, and any building or unit identifiers.

attributes.name: time_zone

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this refinery master record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: vdu_unit_count
attributes.description: Number of vacuum distillation units installed at the refinery. VDUs further process atmospheric residue from CDUs under vacuum to extract additional valuable products.

attributes.name: working_interest_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of ownership interest held by Oil Gas in the refinery facility. Used for financial reporting, cost allocation, and revenue distribution in joint venture arrangements.

products.name: process_unit
products.description: Master record and SSOT for refinery process unit configuration and alarm management. Covers CDU, VDU, FCC, HDS, hydrocracker, reformer, alkylation, isomerization, coker, and treating units. Captures unit type, design capacity, feed type, operating pressure and temperature design limits, capacity constraints, DCS tag prefix, PI System historian tag group, Aspen HYSYS model reference, commissioning date, current operational status, and process alarm management including alarm tags, types (high/low/deviation/rate-of-change), priorities, acknowledgment and shelving status, operator response tracking, and root cause classification per ISA-18.2 alarm management standards and OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119 PSM requirements.

attributes.name: process_unit_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the refinery process unit. Primary key.

attributes.name: joa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.joa. Business justification: Process units in JV refineries need JOA linkage for unit-level capital project approvals, turnaround AFE authorization, and partner cost sharing. JOA voting thresholds apply to major unit modification

attributes.name: psa_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.psa. Business justification: Process units in PSA-operated refineries process PSA-sourced crude; unit-level throughput and yield data feed directly into PSA cost recovery and profit oil calculations. Linking process_unit to PSA e

attributes.name: refinery_id
attributes.description: FK to refining.refinery.refinery_id — MUST-HAVE: Enables linking process units to their parent refinery for capacity planning, turnaround scheduling, and yield optimization. Fundamental parent-child relationship.

attributes.name: active_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this process unit record is currently active in the system.

attributes.name: alarm_acknowledgment_status
attributes.description: Current acknowledgment state of the alarm indicating whether it has been seen and acted upon by an operator.

attributes.name: alarm_priority
attributes.description: Priority level assigned to the alarm indicating urgency of operator response required.

attributes.name: alarm_root_cause_classification
attributes.description: Categorization of the underlying cause of the alarm for trend analysis and continuous improvement (e.g., equipment malfunction, process upset, operator error, design issue).

attributes.name: alarm_setpoint
attributes.description: Threshold value at which the alarm is triggered.

attributes.name: alarm_shelving_expiry_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the alarm shelving will automatically expire and the alarm will be re-enabled.

attributes.name: alarm_shelving_reason
attributes.description: Business justification for shelving the alarm, required for audit and compliance purposes.

attributes.name: alarm_shelving_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the alarm has been temporarily suppressed (shelved) to prevent nuisance alarms during abnormal operations.

attributes.name: alarm_tag
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the process alarm in the DCS or alarm management system.

attributes.name: alarm_type
attributes.description: Classification of the alarm based on the condition being monitored (high limit, low limit, deviation from setpoint, rate of change, equipment failure, or safety-critical event).

attributes.name: aspen_hysys_model_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier to the Aspen HYSYS process simulation model for this unit used for optimization and planning.

attributes.name: capacity_constraint_description
attributes.description: Description of any operational constraints that limit the unit from achieving design capacity (e.g., downstream bottleneck, feedstock quality, equipment degradation).

attributes.name: capacity_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the design capacity. BPD (Barrels Per Day), BOPD (Barrels of Oil Per Day), MCFD (Thousand Cubic Feet per Day), MMCFD (Million Cubic Feet per Day), MT/Day (Metric Tons per Day).

attributes.name: commissioning_date
attributes.description: Date when the process unit was commissioned and placed into service.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this process unit record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: dcs_tag_prefix
attributes.description: Standard tag prefix used in the DCS for all control points and instruments associated with this process unit.

attributes.name: design_capacity
attributes.description: Maximum throughput capacity of the process unit as designed, measured in barrels per day (BPD) for liquid units or thousand cubic feet per day (MCFD) for gas units.
attributes.references: API RP 750 - Process Unit Design Specifications

attributes.name: design_pressure_psi
attributes.description: Maximum operating pressure for which the process unit is designed, measured in pounds per square inch (PSI).
attributes.references: ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section VIII

attributes.name: design_temperature_f
attributes.description: Maximum operating temperature for which the process unit is designed, measured in degrees Fahrenheit.
attributes.references: ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Section VIII

attributes.name: epa_reporting_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Reporting Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this process unit is subject to EPA emissions reporting requirements.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 60 - Standards of Performance for New Stationary Sources

attributes.name: feed_type
attributes.description: Primary feedstock type processed by this unit (e.g., crude oil, vacuum gas oil, naphtha, heavy gas oil).

attributes.name: last_turnaround_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent planned shutdown for major maintenance, inspection, and equipment replacement.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this process unit record was last modified.

attributes.name: next_turnaround_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next planned turnaround maintenance event.

attributes.name: operating_pressure_max_psi
attributes.description: Maximum safe operating pressure for the process unit in pounds per square inch (PSI).

attributes.name: operating_pressure_min_psi
attributes.description: Minimum safe operating pressure for the process unit in pounds per square inch (PSI).

attributes.name: operating_temperature_max_f
attributes.description: Maximum safe operating temperature for the process unit in degrees Fahrenheit.

attributes.name: operating_temperature_min_f
attributes.description: Minimum safe operating temperature for the process unit in degrees Fahrenheit.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the process unit indicating whether it is actively processing, under maintenance, or offline.
attributes.references: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.119 PSM - Process Status Tracking

attributes.name: operator_response_action
attributes.description: Description of the corrective action taken by the operator in response to the alarm.

attributes.name: operator_response_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this alarm requires mandatory operator action or is informational only.

attributes.name: operator_response_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the operator responded to the alarm.

attributes.name: pi_historian_tag_group
attributes.description: OSIsoft PI System tag group identifier for real-time and historical process data collection from this unit.

attributes.name: process_safety_management_tier
attributes.description: Classification of the process unit based on process safety risk and regulatory requirements under OSHA PSM standards.

attributes.name: unit_code
attributes.description: Standardized alphanumeric code for the process unit used across systems and documentation.

attributes.name: unit_name
attributes.description: Business name of the process unit (e.g., CDU-1, FCC-A, HDS-North).
attributes.references: API RP 750 - Refinery Process Unit Naming

attributes.name: unit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the refinery process unit. CDU (Crude Distillation Unit), VDU (Vacuum Distillation Unit), FCC (Fluid Catalytic Cracking), HDS (Hydrodesulfurization), and other major refining process types. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CDU|VDU|FCC|HDS|Hydrocracker|Reformer|Alkylation|Isomerization|Coker|Treating — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

products.name: crude_assay
products.description: Master reference record and SSOT for crude oil grade characterization, including API gravity, sulfur content (wt%), TAN (Total Acid Number), viscosity, pour point, distillation curve (TBP/ASTM D86), metal content (Ni, V, Fe), salt content, Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP), SARA fractions, and yield potential by cut. Linked to crude grade in the product domain. Used by Aspen HYSYS for feedstock blending optimization and CDU/VDU simulation. Each assay represents a specific crude grade's quality profile used for crude valuation, blend optimization, and unit yield prediction.

attributes.name: crude_assay_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the crude assay record. Primary key for the crude assay master data product.

attributes.name: assay_vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to procurement.vendor. Business justification: Crude assays are conducted by specialized external laboratories (Core Laboratories, Intertek). crude_assay.assay_laboratory is a denormalized vendor reference. A proper FK enables laboratory vendor qu

attributes.name: crude_grade_id
attributes.description: Reference to the crude oil grade that this assay characterizes. Links to the crude grade master in the product domain.

attributes.name: lease_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to land.lease. Business justification: Crude assays are routinely performed on lease-specific crude to characterize feedstock quality for refinery planning, crude valuation, and blend optimization. Lease-level assay traceability is standar

attributes.name: pvt_analysis_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reservoir.pvt_analysis. Business justification: Crude assay and PVT analysis are complementary fluid characterization studies on the same reservoir fluid. Refiners correlate assay distillation data with upstream PVT (GOR, shrinkage, bubble point) f

attributes.name: refinery_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to refining.refinery. Business justification: A crude assay is conducted for a specific refinery's feedstock planning and CDU optimization. Linking crude_assay to refinery enables refinery-specific assay libraries and supports crude selection dec

attributes.name: reservoir_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reservoir.reservoir. Business justification: Crude assay characterizes fluid properties of crude sourced from a specific reservoir. Refiners use reservoir-linked assays for feedstock planning, crude compatibility studies, and integrated asset mo

attributes.name: reservoir_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reservoir.zone. Business justification: In commingled or multi-zone production, crude assay properties vary by producing zone. Linking assay to reservoir zone enables zone-specific crude quality tracking, critical for refinery crude slate o

attributes.name: source_drilling_well_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to drilling.drilling_well. Business justification: Drill stem test (DST) samples from a specific drilling_well are sent to labs for crude assay to characterize feedstock before field development. Refiners use well-specific assays for LP optimization a

attributes.name: source_field_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.field. Business justification: Field-level crude assays characterize the aggregate crude quality from a production field and are the primary reference used in refinery crude slate planning and blending optimization. Refiners mainta

attributes.name: source_production_well_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.production_well. Business justification: Crude assays are performed on samples taken from specific production wells. Well-specific assay data is used for reservoir characterization, crude quality tracking, and refinery blending optimization.

attributes.name: api_gravity
attributes.description: API gravity of the crude oil, measured in degrees API. Key indicator of crude density and quality; higher API gravity indicates lighter, more valuable crude. Typical range 10-50 degrees API.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11.1 - Volume Correction Factors

attributes.name: aromatic_content_wt_pct
attributes.description: Aromatic hydrocarbon content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent (from SARA analysis: Saturates, Aromatics, Resins, Asphaltenes). Aromatic content affects product quality (cetane, smoke point) and processing severity requirements.
attributes.references: ASTM D2007 - Standard Test Method for Characteristic Groups in Rubber Extender and Processing Oils by the Clay-Gel Absorption Chromatographic Method (SARA Analysis)

attributes.name: asphaltene_content_wt_pct
attributes.description: Asphaltene content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent. Asphaltenes are heavy, polar molecules that cause fouling, coking, and stability issues. High asphaltene content affects crude compatibility for blending and requires careful processing.
attributes.references: ASTM D6560 - Standard Test Method for Determination of Asphaltenes (Heptane Insolubles) in Crude Petroleum and Petroleum Products

attributes.name: assay_date
attributes.description: Date when the crude oil sample was assayed or when the assay data was published. Used for assay currency and validity tracking.
attributes.references: ASTM D4057 - Standard Practice for Manual Sampling of Petroleum and Petroleum Products

attributes.name: assay_name
attributes.description: Business name or identifier for this crude assay, typically including crude grade name and source location (e.g., 'Brent North Sea 2023', 'WTI Cushing Q1').

attributes.name: assay_report_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or document identifier for the detailed crude assay laboratory report. Links to the full assay documentation including all test results and distillation curves.

attributes.name: assay_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the assay record. Active assays are used for refinery planning and optimization; superseded assays are retained for historical analysis.

attributes.name: assay_version
attributes.description: Version identifier for this assay. Crude assays are updated periodically as crude quality varies; version tracks the iteration.

attributes.name: carbon_residue_wt_pct
attributes.description: Conradson Carbon Residue (CCR) of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent. Indicates coke-forming tendency and asphaltene content. High CCR crude yields more residue and requires coking or residue upgrading capacity. Used for FCC feed quality assessment.
attributes.references: ASTM D189 - Standard Test Method for Conradson Carbon Residue of Petroleum Products; ASTM D4530 - Standard Test Method for Determination of Carbon Residue (Micro Method)

attributes.name: cetane_index
attributes.description: Calculated cetane index of the diesel fraction from the crude assay. Indicates diesel ignition quality; higher cetane index means better diesel quality. Used for crude valuation and diesel blending optimization.
attributes.references: ASTM D976 - Standard Test Method for Calculated Cetane Index of Distillate Fuels; ASTM D4737 - Standard Test Method for Calculated Cetane Index by Four Variable Equation

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this crude assay record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.

attributes.name: diesel_yield_vol_pct
attributes.description: Volume percent yield of diesel cut (typically 520-650°F / 271-343°C) from crude distillation. Diesel is a high-value middle distillate product; yield is a key crude valuation factor.
attributes.references: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

attributes.name: distillation_method
attributes.description: Laboratory distillation method used to generate the crude assay distillation curve. TBP (True Boiling Point) provides the most detailed cut-by-cut yield data for refinery simulation. ASTM D86 is a simpler atmospheric distillation. ASTM D2892 and D5236 are standard crude assay distillation methods.
attributes.references: ASTM D2892 - Standard Test Method for Distillation of Crude Petroleum (15-Theoretical Plate Column); ASTM D5236 - Standard Test Method for Distillation of Heavy Hydrocarbon Mixtures (Vacuum Potstill Method)

attributes.name: flash_point_c
attributes.description: Flash point of the crude oil in degrees Celsius. Lowest temperature at which vapors ignite when exposed to an ignition source. Critical for HSE classification, storage tank design, and transportation safety (OSHA, NFPA, DOT regulations).
attributes.references: ASTM D93 - Standard Test Methods for Flash Point by Pensky-Martens Closed Cup Tester; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.106; NFPA 30

attributes.name: freeze_point_c
attributes.description: Freeze point of the kerosene/jet fuel fraction, measured in degrees Celsius. Critical specification for jet fuel to prevent fuel system icing at high altitude. ASTM D1655 Jet A specification requires maximum -40°C freeze point.
attributes.references: ASTM D2386 - Standard Test Method for Freezing Point of Aviation Fuels; ASTM D1655 - Standard Specification for Aviation Turbine Fuels

attributes.name: heavy_naphtha_yield_vol_pct
attributes.description: Volume percent yield of heavy naphtha cut (typically 180-380°F / 82-193°C) from crude distillation. Heavy naphtha is primary feedstock for catalytic reforming to produce high-octane reformate and hydrogen.
attributes.references: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

attributes.name: hydrogen_content_wt_pct
attributes.description: Hydrogen content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent. Higher hydrogen content indicates more paraffinic crude with better product quality potential. Used in refinery hydrogen balance calculations.
attributes.references: ASTM D5291 - Standard Test Methods for Instrumental Determination of Carbon, Hydrogen, and Nitrogen in Petroleum Products and Lubricants

attributes.name: iron_content_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Iron Content in Parts Per Million (ppm)
attributes.description: Iron (Fe) content in the crude oil, measured in parts per million (ppm). Iron indicates contamination from pipelines, storage tanks, or production equipment. High iron content can foul heat exchangers and poison catalysts.
attributes.references: ASTM D5863 - Standard Test Methods for Determination of Nickel, Vanadium, Iron, and Sodium in Crude Oils and Residual Fuels by Flame Atomic Absorption Spectrometry

attributes.name: kerosene_yield_vol_pct
attributes.description: Volume percent yield of kerosene cut (typically 380-520°F / 193-271°C) from crude distillation. Kerosene is feedstock for jet fuel and heating oil production.
attributes.references: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

attributes.name: light_naphtha_yield_vol_pct
attributes.description: Volume percent yield of light naphtha cut (typically C5-180°F / C5-82°C) from crude distillation. Light naphtha is feedstock for isomerization and reforming to produce high-octane gasoline blendstock.
attributes.references: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this crude assay record was last modified. Used for change tracking and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: nickel_content_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Nickel Content in Parts Per Million (ppm)
attributes.description: Nickel (Ni) content in the crude oil, measured in parts per million (ppm). Nickel and vanadium are catalyst poisons in FCC and hydroprocessing units. High-metal crudes require specialized processing or blending to reduce metal content.
attributes.references: ASTM D5863 - Standard Test Methods for Determination of Nickel, Vanadium, Iron, and Sodium in Crude Oils and Residual Fuels by Flame Atomic Absorption Spectrometry

attributes.name: nitrogen_content_wt_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Nitrogen Content in Weight Parts Per Million (wt ppm)
attributes.description: Total nitrogen content of the crude oil, measured in weight ppm. Nitrogen compounds are catalyst poisons in hydrotreating and hydrocracking units and contribute to NOx emissions. High-nitrogen crudes require additional hydrotreating capacity.
attributes.references: ASTM D4629 - Standard Test Method for Trace Nitrogen in Liquid Petroleum Hydrocarbons by Syringe/Inlet Oxidative Combustion and Chemiluminescence Detection

attributes.name: pour_point_c
attributes.description: Pour point of the crude oil in degrees Celsius. Lowest temperature at which the crude will flow under gravity. Critical for cold-weather storage, pipeline transport, and tank heating requirements.
attributes.references: ASTM D97 - Standard Test Method for Pour Point of Petroleum Products

attributes.name: resin_content_wt_pct
attributes.description: Resin content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent (from SARA analysis). Resins are polar compounds that contribute to crude stability and asphaltene solubility. High resin content can cause processing issues.
attributes.references: ASTM D2007 - Standard Test Method for Characteristic Groups in Rubber Extender and Processing Oils by the Clay-Gel Absorption Chromatographic Method (SARA Analysis)

attributes.name: rvp_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) in Pounds per Square Inch (psi)
attributes.description: Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) of the crude oil, measured in psi at 100°F. Indicates volatility and light-end content. High RVP crude requires vapor recovery systems and affects storage tank design. Also used for gasoline blending RVP compliance (EPA seasonal RVP limits).
attributes.references: ASTM D323 - Standard Test Method for Vapor Pressure of Petroleum Products (Reid Method); EPA 40 CFR Part 80 Subpart E - RVP Standards for Gasoline

attributes.name: salt_content_ptb
attributes.business_glossary_term: Salt Content in Pounds per Thousand Barrels (PTB)
attributes.description: Salt content of the crude oil, measured in pounds per thousand barrels (PTB). High salt content causes corrosion and fouling in crude distillation units. Crude desalting targets <1 PTB to protect downstream equipment.
attributes.references: ASTM D3230 - Standard Test Method for Salts in Crude Oil (Electrometric Method); API RP 571 - Damage Mechanisms Affecting Fixed Equipment in the Refining Industry

attributes.name: saturate_content_wt_pct
attributes.description: Saturate (paraffin and naphthene) content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent (from SARA analysis). High saturate content indicates better quality crude with higher diesel and lube oil yield potential.
attributes.references: ASTM D2007 - Standard Test Method for Characteristic Groups in Rubber Extender and Processing Oils by the Clay-Gel Absorption Chromatographic Method (SARA Analysis)

attributes.name: smoke_point_mm
attributes.description: Smoke point of the kerosene fraction, measured in millimeters. Indicates aromatic content and combustion quality of jet fuel. Higher smoke point means lower aromatics and better jet fuel quality. ASTM D1655 jet fuel specification requires minimum 25mm smoke point.
attributes.references: ASTM D1322 - Standard Test Method for Smoke Point of Kerosene and Aviation Turbine Fuel; ASTM D1655 - Standard Specification for Aviation Turbine Fuels

attributes.name: specific_gravity
attributes.description: Specific gravity of the crude oil at 60°F/60°F (dimensionless ratio). Alternative density measure to API gravity, used in some international markets and process simulations.
attributes.references: ASTM D1298 - Standard Test Method for Density, Relative Density, or API Gravity of Crude Petroleum

attributes.name: sulfur_content_wt_pct
attributes.description: Total sulfur content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent. Critical for refinery processing (HDS unit sizing), product quality (diesel/gasoline sulfur specs), and environmental compliance (EPA Tier 3 standards). Sweet crude <0.5%, sour crude >0.5%.
attributes.references: ASTM D4294 - Standard Test Method for Sulfur in Petroleum by Energy Dispersive X-ray Fluorescence; EPA Tier 3 Gasoline Sulfur Standards

attributes.name: tan_mg_koh_per_g
attributes.business_glossary_term: Total Acid Number (TAN) in Milligrams Potassium Hydroxide per Gram (mg KOH/g)
attributes.description: Total Acid Number (TAN) measured in mg KOH/g. Indicates naphthenic acid content; high TAN crude (>0.5) causes corrosion in refinery units (CDU/VDU overhead systems, heat exchangers). Critical for metallurgy selection and corrosion management.
attributes.references: ASTM D664 - Standard Test Method for Acid Number of Petroleum Products by Potentiometric Titration; NACE SP0403 - Avoiding Caustic Stress Corrosion Cracking of Carbon Steel Refinery Equipment

attributes.name: vacuum_residue_yield_vol_pct
attributes.description: Volume percent yield of vacuum residue (typically 1050°F+ / 566°C+) from vacuum distillation. Vacuum residue is the heaviest fraction, used for asphalt, fuel oil, or fed to coking/residue upgrading units. High residue yield reduces refinery margin.
attributes.references: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

attributes.name: vanadium_content_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Vanadium Content in Parts Per Million (ppm)
attributes.description: Vanadium (V) content in the crude oil, measured in parts per million (ppm). Vanadium is a catalyst poison and causes high-temperature corrosion in furnaces and boilers. Critical for FCC catalyst selection and residue upgrading economics.
attributes.references: ASTM D5863 - Standard Test Methods for Determination of Nickel, Vanadium, Iron, and Sodium in Crude Oils and Residual Fuels by Flame Atomic Absorption Spectrometry

attributes.name: vgo_yield_vol_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Vacuum Gas Oil (VGO) Yield Volume Percent (vol%)
attributes.description: Volume percent yield of vacuum gas oil (VGO) cut (typically 650-1050°F / 343-566°C) from vacuum distillation. VGO is primary feedstock for FCC and hydrocracking units to produce gasoline and diesel.
attributes.references: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining; Aspen HYSYS Process Simulation Standards

attributes.name: viscosity_cst_at_100c
attributes.description: Kinematic viscosity of the crude oil at 100°C, measured in centistokes (cSt). Used for viscosity-temperature relationship modeling and high-temperature process unit design.
attributes.references: ASTM D445 - Standard Test Method for Kinematic Viscosity of Transparent and Opaque Liquids

attributes.name: viscosity_cst_at_40c
attributes.description: Kinematic viscosity of the crude oil at 40°C, measured in centistokes (cSt). Affects pumpability, pipeline transport, and heat exchanger design. Heavy crudes have higher viscosity.
attributes.references: ASTM D445 - Standard Test Method for Kinematic Viscosity of Transparent and Opaque Liquids

attributes.name: water_content_vol_pct
attributes.description: Water and sediment content of the crude oil, expressed as volume percent. Affects crude valuation (water is non-saleable), desalter performance, and corrosion risk. Custody transfer specifications typically require <0.5% water.
attributes.references: ASTM D4007 - Standard Test Method for Water and Sediment in Crude Oil by the Centrifuge Method; API MPMS Chapter 10 - Sediment and Water

attributes.name: wax_content_wt_pct
attributes.description: Paraffin wax content of the crude oil, expressed as weight percent. High wax content affects pour point, pipeline flow, and cold-weather operability. Waxy crudes may require heating or dewaxing for transportation and processing.
attributes.references: ASTM D721 - Standard Test Method for Oil Content of Petroleum Waxes

products.name: feedstock_blend
products.description: Planned or actual blend of crude oil grades and intermediate feedstocks fed to a CDU or process unit during a defined processing period. Captures blend recipe (component crude grades, volume fractions, API gravity, sulfur, TAN), planned vs. actual volumes in barrels, blend date, target unit, blending rationale, and quality compliance status. Supports feedstock optimization and crude scheduling workflows.
products.reference: API MPMS Chapter 12 / Aspen HYSYS Blend Optimizer

attributes.name: blending_recipe_id

attributes.name: crude_grade_id

attributes.name: driving_nomination_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.nomination. Business justification: Feedstock blending decisions are driven by customer nominations specifying crude grade, API gravity, sulfur content, and delivery timing. Links blend optimization to contractual commitments and enable

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: Feedstock blending operations are subject to specific regulatory obligations including Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS2) blending requirements and low-carbon fuel standards. Compliance teams track which

attributes.name: pipeline_nomination_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to logistics.pipeline_nomination. Business justification: Feedstock blends may include pipeline-delivered crudes. Nomination tracking, volume confirmation, and crude slate planning require linking blends to pipeline nominations for supply assurance and feeds

attributes.name: process_unit_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the refinery process unit (CDU, VDU, FCC, HDS, or other) that will receive or has received this feedstock blend.

attributes.name: product_specification_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to refining.product_specification. Business justification: Feedstock blending strategies must consider downstream product specification constraints (sulfur limits, octane targets, distillation curves) to ensure regulatory compliance. Links crude slate optimiz

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to venture.psa. Business justification: Under PSA regimes, feedstock blend composition determines cost oil vs. profit oil volume attribution. Refinery planners must reference the PSA to correctly allocate cost recovery crude within the blen

attributes.name: pvt_analysis_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reservoir.pvt_analysis. Business justification: PVT analysis (formation volume factor, GOR, shrinkage) directly informs feedstock blend optimization. Blend engineers use upstream PVT data to predict stock-tank volumes and blend behavior. This link

attributes.name: refinery_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to refining.refinery_schedule. Business justification: A feedstock blend is planned as part of a refinery production schedule. Linking feedstock_blend to refinery_schedule enables schedule-to-blend traceability, supporting LP model validation and schedule

attributes.name: shipment_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to logistics.shipment. Business justification: Feedstock arriving by vessel or truck corresponds to a shipment record. Feedstock quality traceability, crude supply chain reconciliation, and import documentation all require linking the feedstock bl

attributes.name: source_field_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.field. Business justification: Feedstock blend optimization requires field-level crude origin tracking. Field-wide crude quality characteristics (API, sulfur, GOR) drive blending decisions and crude slate optimization. feedstock_bl

attributes.name: source_production_facility_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.production_facility. Business justification: Refineries track facility sources for feedstock blends to manage supply contracts, quality specifications, and integrated logistics. Critical for vertically integrated operators coordinating productio

attributes.name: actual_total_volume_bbl
attributes.description: The actual total volume of the feedstock blend in barrels (BBL) that was processed through the target unit, measured upon completion or during operations.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the refinery operations manager, process engineer, or authorized personnel who approved this feedstock blend for execution.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this feedstock blend was formally approved for execution by authorized refinery personnel.

attributes.name: blend_api_gravity
attributes.description: The weighted average API gravity of the feedstock blend, a measure of petroleum liquid density relative to water. Higher API gravity indicates lighter, less dense crude oil. Calculated based on component crude grades and their volume fractions.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11.1 - Volume Correction Factors

attributes.name: blend_end_date
attributes.description: The date when the feedstock blend processing or feeding to the target unit was completed or is scheduled to complete.

attributes.name: blend_flash_point_c
attributes.description: The weighted average flash point temperature of the feedstock blend in degrees Celsius, the lowest temperature at which vapors will ignite. Critical for HSE compliance and safe handling procedures.
attributes.references: ASTM D93 - Flash Point, OSHA 29 CFR 1910.106

attributes.name: blend_metals_content_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Blend Metals Content in Parts Per Million (PPM)
attributes.description: The weighted average total metals content (vanadium, nickel, iron) of the feedstock blend expressed in parts per million. Metals can cause catalyst deactivation and fouling in refinery process units.

attributes.name: blend_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name or designation for this feedstock blend, used for operational identification and scheduling purposes.

attributes.name: blend_nitrogen_content_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Blend Nitrogen Content in Parts Per Million (PPM)
attributes.description: The weighted average nitrogen content of the feedstock blend expressed in parts per million. Nitrogen compounds can poison catalysts in downstream units such as FCC and hydrotreating units.

attributes.name: blend_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier or code assigned to this feedstock blend for tracking and reference in refinery operations and scheduling systems.

attributes.name: blend_pour_point_c
attributes.description: The weighted average pour point temperature of the feedstock blend in degrees Celsius, representing the lowest temperature at which the blend will flow. Important for storage and transportation planning.

attributes.name: blend_salt_content_ptb
attributes.business_glossary_term: Blend Salt Content in Pounds per Thousand Barrels (PTB)
attributes.description: The weighted average salt content of the feedstock blend expressed in pounds per thousand barrels. High salt content can cause corrosion and fouling in crude distillation units and requires desalting operations.

attributes.name: blend_sediment_content_vol_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Blend Sediment Content in Volume Percent (VOL%)
attributes.description: The weighted average sediment content of the feedstock blend expressed as volume percentage. Sediment can cause fouling and operational issues in refinery equipment.

attributes.name: blend_start_date
attributes.description: The date when the feedstock blend processing or feeding to the target unit began or is scheduled to begin.

attributes.name: blend_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the feedstock blend. Planned indicates the blend recipe is designed but not yet approved, approved indicates ready for execution, in progress indicates currently being blended or fed to the unit, completed indicates the blend has been fully processed, cancelled indicates the blend was terminated before completion, and on hold indicates temporary suspension.

attributes.name: blend_sulfur_content_wt_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Blend Sulfur Content in Weight Percent (WT%)
attributes.description: The weighted average sulfur content of the feedstock blend expressed as weight percentage. Critical for HDS unit planning, EPA emissions compliance, and product quality specifications.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11.1, EPA Clean Air Act

attributes.name: blend_tan
attributes.description: The weighted average Total Acid Number (TAN) of the feedstock blend, measured in milligrams of potassium hydroxide per gram of sample. TAN indicates the acidity and corrosivity of the crude oil, critical for refinery equipment integrity and corrosion management.

attributes.name: blend_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when the feedstock blend was initiated or executed in the refinery operations, representing the principal business event timestamp for this blend.

attributes.name: blend_type
attributes.description: Classification of the feedstock blend based on its purpose and composition. Crude blend represents primary crude oil mixtures, intermediate blend represents processed stream mixtures, feedstock optimization represents cost or yield optimized recipes, emergency blend represents contingency blends, test blend represents experimental formulations, and standard recipe represents pre-approved recurring blends.

attributes.name: blend_viscosity_cst
attributes.description: The weighted average kinematic viscosity of the feedstock blend measured in centistokes at a standard temperature (typically 40°C or 100°C). Viscosity affects pumping, heating, and processing requirements.

attributes.name: blend_water_content_vol_pct
attributes.business_glossary_term: Blend Water Content in Volume Percent (VOL%)
attributes.description: The weighted average water content of the feedstock blend expressed as volume percentage. Water content affects processing efficiency and must be removed through desalting and dehydration operations.

attributes.name: blending_rationale
attributes.description: The primary business driver or reason for creating this specific feedstock blend. Cost optimization indicates minimizing feedstock cost, yield optimization indicates maximizing valuable product yields, quality compliance indicates meeting product specifications, feedstock availability indicates working with available crude grades, contract obligation indicates fulfilling supply agreements, and operational constraint indicates adapting to refinery limitations.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for operational notes, special instructions, quality observations, or other relevant information about this feedstock blend that may be useful for refinery operations and future reference.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this feedstock blend record was first created in the system, used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: estimated_margin_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Margin in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: The estimated gross margin in USD from processing this feedstock blend, calculated as estimated product value minus estimated processing cost. Key metric for blend selection and refinery profitability analysis.

attributes.name: estimated_processing_cost_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Processing Cost in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: The estimated total cost in USD to process this feedstock blend through the target unit, including feedstock acquisition cost, energy consumption, catalyst usage, and operational expenses. Used for economic evaluation and margin analysis.

attributes.name: estimated_product_value_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Estimated Product Value in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: The estimated total market value in USD of the refined products expected from processing this feedstock blend, based on current market prices and target yield slate. Used for margin calculation and economic optimization.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this feedstock blend record was last updated or modified, used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: optimization_score
attributes.description: A calculated score (typically 0-100) representing how well this feedstock blend achieves the blending objectives (cost, yield, quality) compared to alternative blend recipes. Higher scores indicate better optimization performance.

attributes.name: planned_total_volume_bbl
attributes.description: The total planned volume of the feedstock blend in barrels (BBL) to be processed through the target unit during the defined processing period.

attributes.name: quality_compliance_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the feedstock blend meets all required quality specifications and regulatory standards for processing in the target unit. Compliant indicates all specifications met, non-compliant indicates one or more specifications violated, pending review indicates awaiting quality assurance approval, conditionally approved indicates approved with operational restrictions, and requires adjustment indicates blend recipe needs modification.
attributes.references: API Refining Standards, EPA Clean Air Act

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: The name of the operational system that originated this feedstock blend record, such as Aspen HYSYS process simulation system, refinery planning system, or DCS control system.

attributes.name: target_yield_distillates_pct
attributes.description: The target percentage yield of middle distillates (diesel, jet fuel, kerosene) expected from processing this feedstock blend, used for product slate planning.

attributes.name: target_yield_light_ends_pct
attributes.description: The target percentage yield of light ends (LPG, propane, butane) expected from processing this feedstock blend, used for product slate planning and yield optimization.

attributes.name: target_yield_naphtha_pct
attributes.description: The target percentage yield of naphtha expected from processing this feedstock blend, used for gasoline blending and petrochemical feedstock planning.

attributes.name: target_yield_residue_pct
attributes.description: The target percentage yield of residue (heavy fuel oil, asphalt, vacuum residue) expected from processing this feedstock blend, used for downstream unit planning and product slate optimization.

attributes.name: volume_variance_bbl
attributes.description: The difference between planned and actual total volume in barrels, calculated as actual minus planned. Positive values indicate over-processing, negative values indicate under-processing.

products.name: unit_run
products.description: Primary transactional record and SSOT for process unit operational performance and yield accounting. Covers a defined processing period (shift, day, or campaign) capturing actual throughput (BOPD or MCFD), feed rate, operating temperature, pressure, conversion rate, energy consumption (MMBtu), utility consumption, catalyst activity index, run length, DCS/PI System historian reference, and detailed yield accounting by product cut (LPG, naphtha, kerosene, diesel, gas oil, residue) including actual vs. planned output volumes and mass, liquid volume unaccounted for (LVUF), mass balance closure percentage, BOE conversion, and variance to Aspen HYSYS simulation targets. Supports yield optimization, loss accounting, and refinery planning.

attributes.name: unit_run_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the process unit operational run record. Primary key for unit run transactions.
attributes.references: API Recommended Practice 750 - Measurement of Petroleum and its Products

attributes.name: asset_facility_id
attributes.description: Reference to the refinery facility where this unit run occurred.
attributes.references: API Standard 2000 - Venting Atmospheric and Low-Pressure Storage Tanks

attributes.name: cost_center_id

attributes.references: API Standard 510 - Pressure Vessel Inspection Code

attributes.name: feedstock_blend_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to refining.feedstock_blend. Business justification: A unit_run processes a specific feedstock blend through a CDU, FCC, or HDS unit. Linking unit_run to feedstock_blend is essential for yield accounting — the actual yields (captured in refining_yield_r

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to production.production_facility. Business justification: Unit runs process feedstock from specific production facilities. Tracking source production facility on unit runs enables feedstock quality traceability, yield analysis by crude origin, and supply cha

attributes.name: violation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.violation. Business justification: Specific unit runs may directly trigger compliance violations (emission exceedances, throughput limit breaches, temperature excursions beyond permit limits). Linking unit_run to violation enables root

attributes.name: api_gravity
attributes.description: API gravity of the feedstock or product indicating density and quality classification per API standards.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 11

attributes.name: catalyst_activity_index
attributes.description: Measure of catalyst performance and activity level during the run, typically expressed as percentage of fresh catalyst activity.

attributes.name: catalyst_age_days
attributes.description: Number of days the catalyst has been in service at the time of this run for catalyst lifecycle management.

attributes.name: conversion_rate_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of feedstock converted to lighter products during the run, key performance indicator for cracking units (FCC, hydrocracker).
