attributes.description: System timestamp when this unit run record was first created in the data platform for audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: dcs_historian_tag
attributes.description: Reference tag identifier in the DCS or PI System historian linking to real-time process data for this run.

attributes.name: diesel_yield_bbl
attributes.description: Volume of diesel product cut produced during the run measured in barrels for yield accounting.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 11

attributes.name: electricity_consumption_mwh
attributes.description: Total electrical energy consumed during the run measured in megawatt hours for utility tracking.
attributes.references: API Standard 540 - Electrical Installations in Petroleum Processing Plants

attributes.name: energy_consumption_mmbtu
attributes.business_glossary_term: Energy Consumption Million British Thermal Units (MMBtu)
attributes.description: Total energy consumed during the unit run measured in million British thermal units for energy efficiency analysis.
attributes.references: API Standard 560 - Fired Heaters for General Refinery Service

attributes.name: feed_rate_bopd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Feed Rate Barrels of Oil Per Day (BOPD)
attributes.description: Average feedstock processing rate during the run expressed in barrels of oil per day for throughput analysis.

attributes.name: feedstock_mass_mt
attributes.description: Total mass of feedstock processed during the run measured in metric tons for mass balance calculations.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 11

attributes.name: feedstock_type
attributes.description: Classification of the crude oil or intermediate feedstock processed during this run (e.g., WTI, Brent, heavy sour, light sweet).

attributes.name: feedstock_volume_bbl
attributes.description: Total volume of feedstock processed during the run measured in barrels at standard conditions.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 11 - Physical Properties Data

attributes.name: gas_oil_yield_bbl
attributes.description: Volume of gas oil product cut produced during the run measured in barrels for yield accounting.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 11

attributes.name: kerosene_yield_bbl
attributes.description: Volume of kerosene product cut produced during the run measured in barrels for yield accounting.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 11

attributes.name: liquid_volume_unaccounted_for_bbl
attributes.description: Difference between feedstock input volume and total product output volume, representing measurement uncertainty and losses.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 12 - Calculation of Petroleum Quantities

attributes.name: lpg_yield_bbl
attributes.description: Volume of LPG product cut produced during the run measured in barrels for yield accounting.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 14 - Natural Gas Fluids Measurement

attributes.name: mass_balance_closure_percent
attributes.description: Percentage representing the ratio of total product mass to feedstock mass, indicating accuracy of mass accounting (target: 99-101%).
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 12

attributes.name: naphtha_yield_bbl
attributes.description: Volume of naphtha product cut produced during the run measured in barrels for yield accounting.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 11

attributes.name: operating_pressure_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Operating Pressure Pounds per Square Inch (PSI)
attributes.description: Average operating pressure of the process unit during the run measured in pounds per square inch.
attributes.references: API Standard 510 - Pressure Vessel Inspection Code

attributes.name: operating_temperature_c
attributes.description: Average operating temperature of the process unit during the run measured in degrees Celsius.
attributes.references: API Standard 530 - Calculation of Heater-Tube Thickness in Petroleum Refineries

attributes.name: planned_throughput_bbl
attributes.description: Target feedstock volume planned for this run based on refinery scheduling and optimization models.

attributes.name: residue_yield_bbl
attributes.description: Volume of residue product cut produced during the run measured in barrels for yield accounting.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 11

attributes.name: ron_value
attributes.description: Research octane number of gasoline product cuts indicating anti-knock quality and blending value.
attributes.references: ASTM D2699 - Standard Test Method for Research Octane Number of Spark-Ignition Engine Fuel

attributes.name: run_duration_hours
attributes.description: Total elapsed time of the unit run in hours, calculated from start to end timestamp for cycle time analysis.

attributes.name: run_end_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the unit run processing period ended, marking the completion of the operational cycle.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 21

attributes.name: run_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the unit run, typically formatted as facility-unit-date-sequence for operational tracking and reporting.

attributes.name: run_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the unit run processing period began, marking the start of feedstock introduction to the unit.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 21 - Flow Measurement Using Electronic Metering Systems

attributes.name: run_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the unit run indicating operational state and data completeness.
attributes.references: API Standard 2610 - Design, Construction, Operation, Maintenance, and Inspection of Terminal and Tank Facilities

attributes.name: run_type
attributes.description: Classification of the operational run mode indicating the nature of the processing period.
attributes.references: API Recommended Practice 571 - Damage Mechanisms Affecting Fixed Equipment in the Refining Industry

attributes.name: steam_consumption_mt
attributes.description: Total steam utility consumed during the run measured in metric tons for utility cost allocation.

attributes.name: sulfur_content_ppm
attributes.description: Average sulfur content in the feedstock or product measured in parts per million for HDS unit performance and EPA compliance.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act - Tier 3 Gasoline Sulfur Standards

attributes.name: tan_mg_koh_per_g
attributes.business_glossary_term: Total Acid Number (TAN) Milligrams Potassium Hydroxide per Gram (mg KOH/g)
attributes.description: Total acid number of the feedstock or product measured in mg KOH per gram, indicating corrosivity and processing requirements.
attributes.references: ASTM D664 - Standard Test Method for Acid Number of Petroleum Products by Potentiometric Titration

attributes.name: throughput_variance_bbl
attributes.description: Difference between actual and planned throughput volumes, indicating operational performance against plan.

attributes.name: total_output_boe
attributes.business_glossary_term: Total Output Barrel of Oil Equivalent (BOE)
attributes.description: Total production output normalized to barrel of oil equivalent for standardized reporting and comparison.

attributes.name: total_product_mass_mt
attributes.description: Sum of all product cut masses produced during the run measured in metric tons for mass balance closure.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 11

attributes.name: total_product_volume_bbl
attributes.description: Sum of all product cut volumes produced during the run measured in barrels for overall yield verification.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: System timestamp when this unit run record was last modified for change tracking and data lineage.

products.name: yield_record
products.description: Detailed yield accounting record for a process unit run, capturing actual output volumes and mass by product cut (LPG, naphtha, kerosene, diesel, gas oil, residue, etc.) against planned yield targets. Includes liquid volume unaccounted for (LVUF), mass balance closure percentage, BOE conversion, and variance to Aspen HYSYS simulation targets. Supports yield optimization, loss accounting, and refinery planning.
products.reference: API MPMS Chapter 19 / COPAS Yield Accounting

attributes.name: lvuf_bbl

attributes.name: mass_variance_mt
attributes.description: Difference between actual and planned mass (actual minus planned), measured in metric tons. Used for yield optimization and loss accounting.

attributes.name: measurement_method
attributes.description: Method used to measure or calculate the yield volumes and masses. Impacts data quality and uncertainty levels.

attributes.name: planned_volume_bbl

attributes.name: quality_grade

attributes.name: reconciliation_notes

attributes.name: ron_value

attributes.name: yield_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage yield of this product cut relative to total feedstock input. Calculated as (product volume / feedstock volume) * 100.

attributes.name: yield_status

attributes.description: Calculated deviation of the measured value from the specification limit (positive indicates above max or below min, negative indicates within spec with margin). Used for quality trending and early warning of specification drift.

attributes.name: epa_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this test result is used for EPA regulatory compliance reporting (e.g., sulfur content for Clean Air Act compliance, benzene content for air toxics regulations). True indicates EPA-reportable test; False indicates internal quality control only.
attributes.references: EPA Clean Air Act - Fuel Quality Standards

attributes.name: laboratory_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the laboratory that performed the test (e.g., refinery on-site lab, third-party contract lab, regional quality center). Used for lab performance tracking and inter-laboratory comparison.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - General Requirements for the Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories

attributes.name: measured_value
attributes.description: Numerical result of the laboratory test for the specified property. Precision varies by test method and property type. Used for specification compliance checking and quality trending.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - General Requirements for the Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this quality test record was last modified. Used for change tracking, audit trail, and data quality monitoring.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - General Requirements for the Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories

attributes.name: quality_control_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this test record represents a quality control sample (e.g., blind duplicate, spiked sample, reference standard) rather than a production sample. True indicates QC sample; False indicates production sample.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - General Requirements for the Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories

attributes.name: retest_reason
attributes.description: Explanation of why a retest was required, such as 'Result outside expected range', 'Instrument calibration failure', 'Sample contamination suspected', or 'Quality control check failed'. Used for laboratory quality improvement.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - General Requirements for the Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories

attributes.name: retest_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the sample requires retesting due to questionable results, instrument malfunction, or quality control failure. True indicates retest is required; False indicates result is accepted.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - General Requirements for the Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories

attributes.name: sample_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the physical sample was collected from the process unit, storage tank, or pipeline. Critical for correlating test results with production conditions and process parameters at the time of sampling.

attributes.name: sample_point_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the physical location where the sample was collected, such as unit outlet, tank number, pipeline tap, or blending header. Enables spatial analysis of quality variation across the refinery.
attributes.references: API RP 500 - Recommended Practice for Classification of Locations for Electrical Installations at Petroleum Facilities

attributes.name: sample_point_description
attributes.description: Human-readable description of the sample collection location, including process unit name, equipment tag, and stream description (e.g., 'CDU Overhead Naphtha', 'FCC Gasoline Blending Header', 'Tank 101 Diesel Product').
attributes.references: API RP 500 - Recommended Practice for Classification of Locations for Electrical Installations at Petroleum Facilities

attributes.name: specification_max
attributes.description: Maximum acceptable value for the tested property per the product grade specification. Null if no maximum limit applies. Used for automated pass/fail determination.
attributes.references: ASTM D4814 - Standard Specification for Automotive Spark-Ignition Engine Fuel

attributes.name: specification_min
attributes.description: Minimum acceptable value for the tested property per the product grade specification. Null if no minimum limit applies. Used for automated pass/fail determination.
attributes.references: ASTM D4814 - Standard Specification for Automotive Spark-Ignition Engine Fuel

attributes.name: specification_target
attributes.description: Target or typical value for the tested property, representing the optimal quality aim for process control. May differ from regulatory limits to provide operating margin and reduce giveaway.
attributes.references: API RP 750 - Management of Process Hazards

attributes.name: test_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the laboratory analysis was performed. Used to track laboratory turnaround time and ensure test results are within validity windows for time-sensitive properties.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - General Requirements for the Competence of Testing and Calibration Laboratories

attributes.name: test_method_code
attributes.description: Standardized test method code used for the analysis (e.g., 'ASTM D2699' for RON, 'ASTM D86' for distillation, 'ASTM D4294' for sulfur, 'IP 365' for flash point). Ensures reproducibility and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: ASTM International Standards - Petroleum Products and Lubricants

attributes.name: test_method_description
attributes.description: Full description of the test method standard, including the property being measured and the analytical technique (e.g., 'ASTM D2699 - Research Octane Number of Spark-Ignition Engine Fuel', 'ASTM D5453 - Sulfur by Ultraviolet Fluorescence').
attributes.references: ASTM International Standards - Petroleum Products and Lubricants

attributes.name: test_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the quality test, typically assigned by the laboratory information management system (LIMS) or refinery quality control system. Used for external reference and tracking.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14 - Natural Gas Fluids Measurement

attributes.name: test_precision
attributes.description: Repeatability or reproducibility precision of the test method as defined by the standard method (e.g., ASTM precision statement). Used to assess measurement uncertainty and determine if differences are statistically significant.
attributes.references: ASTM E691 - Standard Practice for Conducting an Interlaboratory Study to Determine the Precision of a Test Method

attributes.name: test_property_name
attributes.description: Name of the physical or chemical property being measured (e.g., 'Research Octane Number', 'Sulfur Content', 'Flash Point', 'Viscosity', 'Density', 'Cloud Point', 'Pour Point', 'Reid Vapor Pressure', 'Total Acid Number').
attributes.references: API Technical Data Book - Petroleum Refining

attributes.name: test_result_status
attributes.description: Overall pass/fail status of the test result against specification limits. 'Pass' indicates all properties meet specifications; 'Fail' indicates one or more properties are out of specification; 'Conditional' indicates marginal results requiring review; 'Retest' indicates sample requires re-analysis; 'Pending' indicates test in progress; 'Cancelled' indicates test was voided.

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the test result (e.g., 'octane number' for RON/MON, 'ppm' for sulfur, 'deg C' for flash point, 'cSt' for viscosity, 'kg/m3' for density, 'psi' for RVP, 'mg KOH/g' for TAN). Essential for correct interpretation and comparison.

products.name: refinery_schedule

Integrates with Aspen HYSYS LP optimization.

attributes.name: naphtha_target_volume_bbl

attributes.name: planned_margin_usd

attributes.name: planning_period_end_date

attributes.name: planning_period_start_date

attributes.name: product_slate_plan

attributes.name: resolution_status
attributes.description: Current status of corrective actions for schedule deviations. Tracks progress from identification through resolution.

attributes.name: schedule_number
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the refinery production schedule, used for cross-system reference and communication with operations teams.

attributes.name: schedule_status

attributes.name: schedule_type
attributes.description: Classification of the schedule by planning horizon and frequency. Determines the granularity and scope of the production plan.

attributes.name: schedule_version

attributes.name: superseded_timestamp

products.name: blending_recipe
products.description: Master record and SSOT for petroleum product blending specifications and blending execution history. Used by Aspen HYSYS blend optimizer and DCS blend controllers. Supports product release, quality certification, and blend loss accounting.

attributes.name: target_density_kg_m3

Used as the authoritative quality target for product blending, quality testing pass/fail determination, and product release certification.
products.reference: ASTM D4814 / EN 228 / EPA Tier 3 / IMO MARPOL Annex VI

attributes.name: product_specification_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the product specification record. Primary key for the product specification master reference.

attributes.name: obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: Product specifications fulfill specific regulatory obligations (EPA Tier 3 sulfur standard, CARB fuel requirements, RFS renewable content). Compliance teams link specifications to obligations to confi

attributes.name: quality_spec_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.quality_spec. Business justification: Internal refinery product specifications must comply with and be traceable to the governing product-level quality_spec (regulatory/market standard). Specification management, regulatory audit, and pro

attributes.name: regulatory_authority_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.regulatory_authority. Business justification: Product specifications are set or approved by regulatory authorities (EPA for Tier 3 fuel standards, CARB for California fuels, EU for EN 590). The existing regulatory_basis column is a denormalized t

attributes.name: superseded_by_specification_product_specification_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specification that supersedes this one. Nullable for active specifications. Used to maintain specification lineage and version history.

attributes.name: api_gravity_max
attributes.description: Maximum API gravity. Upper limit ensures product meets grade specifications and handling characteristics.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11; ASTM D287; ASTM D1298

attributes.name: api_gravity_min
attributes.description: Minimum API gravity. Inverse measure of petroleum liquid density relative to water. Higher API gravity indicates lighter products. Typical range is 45-70 for gasoline, 30-42 for diesel.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 11; ASTM D287; ASTM D1298

attributes.name: applicable_standard
attributes.description: Primary industry or regulatory standard governing this specification. Examples include ASTM D4814 for gasoline, ASTM D975 for diesel, EN 228 for European gasoline, ISO 8217 for marine fuels, API gravity standards.
attributes.references: ASTM International; European Committee for Standardization (CEN); ISO; API

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date when this specification was formally approved for operational use. Part of quality management audit trail.
attributes.references: Quality Management System Standards; ISO 9001; SOX Controls

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the person or role who approved this specification for use. Part of quality management audit trail.
attributes.references: Quality Management System Standards; ISO 9001; SOX Controls

attributes.name: aromatics_max_vol_pct
attributes.description: Maximum aromatic hydrocarbon content by volume percent. Regulated to control emissions and combustion characteristics. EPA and CARB set limits (typically 25-35% for gasoline).
attributes.references: ASTM D1319; ASTM D5769; EPA; CARB

attributes.name: benzene_max_vol_pct
attributes.description: Maximum benzene content by volume percent. Strictly regulated carcinogen. EPA Mobile Source Air Toxics limit is 0.62% average, CARB limit is 0.7% maximum.
attributes.references: ASTM D3606; ASTM D5580; EPA MSAT; CARB

attributes.name: cetane_index_min
attributes.description: Minimum cetane index for diesel fuel. Indicates ignition quality and combustion performance. Typical minimum is 40 for automotive diesel, 47 for premium grades.

attributes.name: cetane_number_min
attributes.description: Minimum cetane number measured by engine test. Direct measure of diesel ignition quality. More accurate than cetane index but more expensive to determine.

attributes.name: cloud_point_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum cloud point temperature in degrees Celsius. Defines low-temperature operability for diesel fuels. Varies by season and geographic market (e.g., -10°C for winter diesel).

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text comments or notes about this specification. May include special handling instructions, seasonal applicability notes, or references to supporting documentation.

attributes.name: copper_strip_corrosion_max
attributes.description: Maximum allowable copper strip corrosion rating. Indicates presence of corrosive sulfur compounds. Typical maximum is 1 for gasoline and diesel, 1 for jet fuel.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this specification record was first created in the system. Part of data lineage and audit trail.
attributes.references: Internal Data Management Standard; SOX Controls

attributes.name: density_max_kg_m3
attributes.description: Maximum density in kilograms per cubic meter at 15°C. Upper limit ensures product meets grade specifications and combustion characteristics.
attributes.references: ASTM D4052; ISO 12185; API MPMS Chapter 11

attributes.name: density_min_kg_m3
attributes.description: Minimum density in kilograms per cubic meter at 15°C. Used for mass-volume conversions and quality control. Typical range is 720-775 kg/m³ for gasoline, 820-845 kg/m³ for diesel.
attributes.references: ASTM D4052; ISO 12185; API MPMS Chapter 11

attributes.name: distillation_fbp_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum final boiling point temperature during distillation. Ensures complete vaporization and limits heavy-end components that contribute to deposits and emissions.

attributes.name: distillation_t10_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum temperature at which 10% of the sample is recovered during distillation. Controls front-end volatility for gasoline and diesel. Affects cold start performance.

attributes.name: distillation_t50_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum temperature at which 50% of the sample is recovered during distillation. Indicates mid-range volatility and affects warm-up performance and vapor lock tendency.

attributes.name: distillation_t90_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum temperature at which 90% of the sample is recovered during distillation. Controls back-end volatility. Affects combustion completeness and deposit formation.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when this specification becomes binding for quality testing and product release. Used to manage specification version transitions and regulatory compliance cutover dates.

attributes.name: ethanol_max_vol_pct
attributes.description: Maximum ethanol content by volume percent. Common blends are E10 (10% ethanol) and E15 (15% ethanol). Affects vapor pressure, phase separation, and materials compatibility.
attributes.references: ASTM D4806; EPA Renewable Fuel Standard

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when this specification is no longer valid for quality testing and product release. Nullable for specifications without a defined end date. Used to manage specification supersession and regulatory phase-outs.

attributes.name: flash_point_min_c
attributes.description: Minimum flash point temperature in degrees Celsius. Safety-critical specification for distillate fuels. Typical minimum is 38°C for diesel and 40°C for jet fuel.
attributes.references: ASTM D93; ASTM D56; API Standards

attributes.name: freeze_point_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum freeze point temperature in degrees Celsius. Critical specification for jet fuel to prevent fuel system icing at altitude. Typical maximum is -40°C for Jet A and -47°C for Jet A-1.
attributes.references: ASTM D1655; ASTM D5972; DEF STAN 91-91

attributes.name: geographic_market
attributes.description: Geographic region or market where this specification applies. Examples include US Gulf Coast, California CARB, European Union, Singapore, specific state markets. Supports regional specification management for products with varying quality requirements by jurisdiction.

attributes.name: lubricity_max_microns
attributes.description: Maximum wear scar diameter in microns measured by High-Frequency Reciprocating Rig (HFRR) test. Critical for ULSD to prevent fuel injection system wear. Typical maximum is 520 microns at 60°C.

attributes.name: mon_min
attributes.description: Minimum Motor Octane Number required for gasoline products. Used in conjunction with RON to determine anti-knock index (AKI). Typical values range from 82 to 92 MON.

attributes.name: olefins_max_vol_pct
attributes.description: Maximum olefin content by volume percent. Affects oxidation stability and deposit formation. CARB limits olefins to 10% for reformulated gasoline.

attributes.name: oxygen_max_wt_pct
attributes.description: Maximum oxygen content by weight percent. Typically from ethanol or MTBE blending. EPA allows up to 3.7% oxygen by weight for conventional gasoline, 2.7% for reformulated gasoline.

attributes.name: particulate_max_mg_l
attributes.description: Maximum particulate contamination in milligrams per liter. Critical for fuel injection system protection. Typical limit is 24 mg/L for diesel.

attributes.name: pour_point_max_c
attributes.description: Maximum pour point temperature in degrees Celsius. Defines the lowest temperature at which the product remains pourable. Critical for fuel oils and lubricants.

attributes.name: product_category
attributes.description: Classification of the product type. Distinguishes between finished refined products ready for market, intermediate streams within the refinery, blendstocks used in blending operations, and feedstocks entering process units.
attributes.references: API Standards; Refinery Operations Best Practices

attributes.name: product_grade
attributes.description: Commercial grade designation of the refined product or intermediate stream. Examples include Regular Unleaded 87, Premium 93, ULSD 15ppm, Jet A-1, RBOB, Reformate, FCC Gasoline.
attributes.references: API Standards; ASTM D4814; ASTM D975; ASTM D1655

attributes.name: product_type
attributes.description: Specific type of petroleum product. Defines the primary product family for quality control and market positioning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: gasoline|diesel|jet_fuel|kerosene|fuel_oil|lpg|naphtha|reformate|fcc_gasoline|alkylate|other — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: ron_min
attributes.description: Minimum Research Octane Number required for gasoline products. Critical quality parameter for gasoline blending and anti-knock performance. Typical values range from 87 to 98 RON.

attributes.name: rvp_max_psi
attributes.business_glossary_term: Reid Vapor Pressure (RVP) Maximum (Pounds per Square Inch)
attributes.description: Maximum Reid Vapor Pressure in pounds per square inch. Controls gasoline volatility and evaporative emissions. EPA and CARB set seasonal and geographic RVP limits (typically 7.0-9.0 psi summer, 13.5-15.0 psi winter).
attributes.references: ASTM D323; EPA Volatility Regulations; CARB

attributes.name: specification_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the product specification. Describes the product grade and quality standard in business terms.

attributes.name: specification_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the product specification. Externally-known unique code used in quality testing, blending operations, and product release documentation.

attributes.name: specification_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the product specification. Active specifications are used for quality testing and product release decisions. Superseded specifications are retained for historical reference.

attributes.name: sulfur_max_ppm
attributes.description: Maximum allowable sulfur content in parts per million. Critical for EPA Tier 3 compliance (10 ppm gasoline), ULSD requirements (15 ppm diesel), and IMO 2020 marine fuel limits (0.5% or 5000 ppm). Drives HDS unit performance requirements.
attributes.references: EPA Tier 3 Standards; ASTM D5453; IMO 2020; CARB

attributes.name: tan_max_mg_koh_per_g
attributes.business_glossary_term: Total Acid Number (TAN) Maximum (Milligrams Potassium Hydroxide per Gram)
attributes.description: Maximum Total Acid Number in milligrams of potassium hydroxide per gram of sample. Measures acidity and corrosivity of crude oil and intermediate streams. High TAN crudes require special metallurgy and processing.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this specification record was last modified. Part of data lineage and audit trail.
attributes.references: Internal Data Management Standard; SOX Controls

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Version number of this specification. Incremented when specification is revised. Supports specification change management and historical tracking.

attributes.name: viscosity_max_cst
attributes.description: Maximum kinematic viscosity in centistokes at specified temperature (typically 40°C). Upper limit ensures proper fuel system operation and combustion efficiency.

attributes.name: viscosity_min_cst
attributes.description: Minimum kinematic viscosity in centistokes at specified temperature (typically 40°C). Defines flow characteristics and atomization performance. Critical for diesel and fuel oils.

attributes.name: water_content_max_ppm
attributes.description: Maximum water content in parts per million. Critical for jet fuel (50 ppm max) and diesel to prevent microbial growth, corrosion, and ice formation.
attributes.references: ASTM D1744; ASTM D6304; ASTM D1655

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to logistics.shipment. Business justification: Spent catalyst is shipped out for regeneration or disposal; fresh catalyst arrives via inbound shipment. Hazmat shipping compliance (DOT/IATA), catalyst regeneration vendor logistics, and turnaround m

attributes.name: catalyst_age_days

attributes.name: catalyst_batch_number
attributes.description: Unique batch or lot number assigned by the manufacturer for traceability and quality control. Critical for tracking performance and warranty claims.

attributes.name: catalyst_grade

attributes.name: coke_content_wt_pct

attributes.name: cumulative_throughput_bbl

attributes.name: current_activity_level
attributes.description: Current catalytic activity level expressed as a percentage of fresh catalyst performance. Declines over time due to fouling, poisoning, and thermal degradation. Critical for determining regeneration or replacement timing.

attributes.name: current_mass
attributes.description: Current mass of active catalyst in the process unit after accounting for additions, withdrawals, and attrition. Used for material balance and performance calculations.
attributes.references: API RP 571 - Damage Mechanisms Affecting Fixed Equipment in the Refining Industry

attributes.name: current_volume

attributes.references: API RP 571 - Damage Mechanisms Affecting Fixed Equipment in the Refining Industry

products.name: crude_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the operational allocation of received crude oil volumes to planned feedstock blends in refinery crude scheduling and feedstock optimization workflows. It captures the explicit business decision to assign a portion of a crude receipt to a specific feedstock blend recipe, including allocated volume, volume fraction, allocation date, and status. Each record links one crude_receipt to one feedstock_blend with attributes that exist only in the context of this allocation decision.. Existence Justification: In refinery operations, a single crude receipt (e.g., a vessel delivery of 500,000 barrels) is routinely split and allocated across multiple feedstock blends targeting different process units or processing periods. Conversely, a single feedstock blend recipe typically draws from multiple crude receipts to achieve the desired quality profile (API gravity, sulfur content, TAN). Crude schedulers actively manage these allocations in refinery planning systems (Aspen PIMS, Spiral) as a distinct operational activity with its own data (allocated volumes, fractions, dates, status).

attributes.name: crude_allocation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the crude allocation record. Primary key for the crude_allocation association product.

attributes.name: crude_receipt_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the crude oil receipt transaction being allocated to a feedstock blend.

attributes.name: feedstock_blend_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to the feedstock blend receiving the allocated crude volume.

attributes.name: allocated_by
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the crude scheduler, process engineer, or planning system user who created this allocation record.

attributes.name: allocated_volume_bbl
attributes.description: The volume of crude oil in barrels allocated from this crude receipt to this feedstock blend. This is the portion of the crude_receipt.net_volume_bbl assigned to this specific blend.

attributes.name: allocation_date
attributes.description: The date when this crude volume was allocated to the feedstock blend by the crude scheduler or refinery planning system.

attributes.name: allocation_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes recorded by the crude scheduler regarding the rationale for this allocation, quality considerations, or operational constraints.

attributes.name: allocation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the crude allocation. Planned indicates the allocation is part of a future blend plan. Confirmed indicates the allocation has been approved. Executed indicates the crude has been physically blended. Cancelled indicates the allocation was reversed.

attributes.name: allocation_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time when this crude allocation record was created in the refinery scheduling system.

attributes.name: volume_fraction_pct
attributes.description: The percentage of the feedstock blend total volume represented by this crude allocation. Used in blend recipe calculations and feedstock optimization.

products.name: schedule_unit_plan
products.description: This association product represents the operational planning assignment between a refinery production schedule and a process unit. It captures the specific throughput targets, operational modes, and maintenance windows that refinery schedulers assign to each process unit within a given planning period. Each record links one refinery_schedule to one process_unit with planning parameters that exist only in the context of that schedule-unit combination, enabling detailed production planning and variance tracking per unit per schedule period.. Existence Justification: In refinery production planning operations, schedulers explicitly create unit-specific operating plans for each process unit within each schedule period. A single refinery schedule (e.g., Q1 2024 production plan) contains distinct throughput targets, operational modes, and maintenance windows for multiple process units (CDU, FCC, HDS, reformer, etc.). Conversely, each process unit participates in multiple schedules over time (monthly, quarterly, annual planning cycles). This is a recognized operational planning artifact in refinery scheduling systems like Aspen PIMS and Honeywell Refinery Planner.

attributes.description: Actual achieved throughput rate for this unit during this schedule period. Enables planned vs. actual variance analysis at the unit level.

attributes.description: Planned daily throughput rate for the Crude Distillation Unit in barrels per day. Key operational target for primary refining capacity utilization. Moving to association enables proper normalization where each unit has its own plan record.]

products.name: hierarchy
products.description: Defines the parent-child hierarchical relationships among assets in the Maximo CMMS asset tree, enabling roll-up of maintenance costs, failure events, and performance metrics from component level up to facility level. Captures parent asset reference, child asset reference, hierarchy level (facility → system → equipment → component), effective date, end date, and hierarchy type (functional location, physical location, or cost-rollup). Supports ISO 55001 asset management structure and SAP PM functional location hierarchy. Essential for organizational reporting and maintenance cost allocation.

attributes.name: depth
attributes.description: Total number of levels from the root asset to the child asset in this relationship. Supports complexity analysis and organizational structure metrics.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the hierarchical relationship became active and valid for operational use. Supports temporal tracking of asset organizational changes, turnarounds, and Management of Change (MOC) workflows.

attributes.name: end_date
attributes.description: Date when the hierarchical relationship was terminated or superseded. Null indicates the relationship is currently active. Supports historical analysis of asset configuration changes and decommissioning tracking.

attributes.name: functional_location_code
attributes.description: SAP Plant Maintenance (PM) functional location identifier representing the process-based organizational position of the child asset within the parent. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA PM module functional location master data.

attributes.name: geographic_location_code
attributes.description: Geographic location identifier for the hierarchical relationship, typically representing field, platform, or facility location. Supports spatial analysis and GIS integration for asset mapping and logistics planning.

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: Numeric depth of the child asset within the organizational hierarchy tree. Level 1 typically represents facility, Level 2 represents system, Level 3 represents equipment, Level 4 represents component. Enables roll-up aggregation and drill-down analysis.

attributes.name: hierarchy_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the hierarchical relationship. attributes.name: hierarchy_type

attributes.name: hse_classification

attributes.references: OSHA PSM, EPA, BSEE Safety Case, API RP 754

attributes.name: planner_group
attributes.description: Maintenance planning group assigned to manage work orders and preventive maintenance schedules for assets in this hierarchical branch. Supports maintenance resource allocation and workload balancing.

attributes.name: primary_hierarchy_flag

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this preventive maintenance plan expires or is retired. Null for open-ended plans.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this preventive maintenance plan becomes active and begins generating scheduled work orders.

attributes.name: environmental_critical_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this preventive maintenance plan is for an environmentally-critical asset or system (e.g., spill containment, emissions control, LDAR equipment) requiring environmental compliance oversight.

attributes.name: estimated_contractor_cost
attributes.description: Estimated third-party contractor cost in USD for this preventive maintenance activity, if external services are required (e.g., specialized inspection, NDT services, equipment rental).

attributes.name: estimated_duration_hours
attributes.description: Estimated time in hours required to complete the preventive maintenance activity, used for scheduling and resource planning.

attributes.name: estimated_labor_cost
attributes.description: Estimated labor cost in USD for executing this preventive maintenance activity, used for budgeting and cost-benefit analysis. Includes craft labor, supervision, and support personnel.

attributes.name: estimated_material_cost
attributes.description: Estimated material and spare parts cost in USD for this preventive maintenance activity, used for budgeting and inventory planning.

attributes.name: frequency_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the frequency interval: calendar units (days, weeks, months, years) or usage-based units (operating hours, cycles, barrels processed, cubic feet produced). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: days|weeks|months|years|operating_hours|cycles|barrels_processed|cubic_feet_produced — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: frequency_value
attributes.description: Numeric value representing the interval between preventive maintenance activities. Interpreted in conjunction with frequency_unit (e.g., 30 for 30 days, 500 for 500 operating hours).

attributes.name: last_completed_date
attributes.description: The date when the most recent preventive maintenance work order generated from this plan was completed.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this preventive maintenance plan record was last updated or revised.

attributes.name: maintenance_strategy_type
attributes.description: The governing maintenance strategy philosophy for this plan: run-to-failure (reactive), time-based (fixed interval), condition-based (triggered by condition monitoring), predictive (using analytics/AI), reliability-centered (RCM methodology), or risk-based (prioritized by risk assessment).
attributes.references: ISO 55001 Asset Management, Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) SAE JA1011

attributes.name: mean_time_between_failures
attributes.description: Historical or target Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) in hours for the asset covered by this preventive maintenance plan, used to optimize maintenance intervals and assess reliability improvement.

attributes.name: mean_time_to_repair
attributes.description: Historical or target Mean Time To Repair (MTTR) in hours for the asset covered by this preventive maintenance plan, used for downtime planning and resource allocation.

attributes.name: moc_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether execution of this preventive maintenance plan requires a formal Management of Change (MOC) review due to potential impact on process safety, equipment design, or operating procedures.

attributes.name: next_scheduled_date
attributes.description: The next calendar date when a preventive maintenance work order is scheduled to be generated based on this plan.

attributes.name: plan_code
attributes.description: Externally-known unique business identifier for the preventive maintenance plan, used for reference in Maximo CMMS and operational documentation.

attributes.name: plan_name
attributes.description: Human-readable descriptive name of the preventive maintenance plan.

attributes.name: plan_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the preventive maintenance plan: active (generating work orders), inactive (not generating work orders), suspended (temporarily paused), under_review (being revised), or obsolete (retired).

attributes.name: priority_level
attributes.description: Business priority level for this preventive maintenance plan, reflecting the criticality of the asset and the consequence of maintenance deferral.

attributes.name: ptw_required_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether execution of this preventive maintenance activity requires a formal Permit to Work (PTW) due to hazardous conditions (e.g., hot work, confined space entry, energized electrical work, work at height).

attributes.name: rcm_analysis_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) analysis document or study that supports the maintenance strategy and frequency defined in this plan.

attributes.name: regulatory_inspection_requirement
attributes.description: Applicable regulatory inspection standards and requirements that this preventive maintenance plan must satisfy (e.g., BSEE offshore inspection, PHMSA pipeline integrity, API RP 510 pressure vessel inspection, API RP 570 piping inspection, API RP 653 storage tank inspection).
attributes.references: BSEE, PHMSA, API RP 510, API RP 570, API RP 653

attributes.name: required_craft_skills
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of craft skills or trade qualifications required to execute this preventive maintenance plan (e.g., Instrumentation Technician, Mechanical Fitter, Electrical Engineer, NDT Inspector, API 510 Inspector).
attributes.references: Maximo Asset Management, OSHA Training Requirements

attributes.name: safety_critical_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this preventive maintenance plan is for a safety-critical asset or system (e.g., BOP, pressure relief valve, fire suppression system, H2S detection system) requiring heightened oversight and compliance.

attributes.name: spare_parts_list
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of spare part numbers or material codes required for this preventive maintenance activity, used for inventory planning and procurement.

attributes.name: task_list_reference
attributes.description: Reference to the detailed task list or job plan in Maximo CMMS that defines the step-by-step procedures, safety precautions, and quality checks for this preventive maintenance activity.

attributes.name: trigger_type
attributes.description: The mechanism that triggers work order generation: calendar (time-based schedule), meter (usage-based such as operating hours or cycles), condition (threshold breach from monitoring), or hybrid (combination of triggers).

attributes.name: turnaround_planning_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this preventive maintenance activity is part of a planned turnaround or major shutdown event, requiring coordination with production scheduling and multi-discipline planning.

attributes.name: work_order_type
attributes.description: The Maximo work order type code that will be assigned to work orders generated from this preventive maintenance plan (e.g., PM, INSP, CALIB, LUBE).

products.name: integrity_program
products.description: Defines the ISO 55001-aligned asset integrity management program for each asset or asset class, including program type (corrosion management, fatigue management, pressure containment, structural integrity), applicable standards (API, ASME, NACE), inspection strategy, risk-based inspection (RBI) methodology, acceptable risk threshold, program owner, regulatory basis, and corrosion monitoring location (CML) registry with nominal/minimum thickness, monitoring method, corrosion rates, and remaining life calculations. Serves as the governing framework that drives inspection plans, monitoring programs, and fitness-for-service assessments across the asset portfolio. Supports PHMSA pipeline integrity management and API RP 570/580/581 compliance.

domains.name: logistics
domains.description: Manages transportation and movement of crude oil, natural gas, LNG, LPG, NGLs, and refined products across pipelines, tankers, trucks, and rail. Owns shipping schedules, pipeline nominations, FPSO liftings, custody transfer records, tariff rates, delivery scheduling, and carrier management. Aligns with PHMSA pipeline safety regulations and FERC tariff reporting requirements. Integrates with SCADA pipeline monitoring systems.

products.name: shipment
products.description: Core master entity representing a discrete movement of petroleum products (crude oil, LNG, LPG, NGLs, refined products) from origin to destination across all transport modes. Captures shipment reference number, cargo type, product grade, nominated and actual volumes (BOE/BBL/MMCFD), origin and destination terminals or facilities, transport mode (pipeline, tanker, truck, rail, FPSO lifting), scheduled and actual departure/arrival timestamps, shipment status, carrier assignment, bill of lading or waybill number, custody transfer status, INCOTERMS, and mode-specific detail records: for truck — driver ID, truck registration, loading rack, gross/net volume, API gravity, temperature, BS&W, seal numbers, ticket number; for rail — railroad SCAC code, car initial and number, UN hazmat number, number of cars, gross/net weight, hazmat placard requirements, waybill number and status; for marine — voyage reference. Serves as the SSOT for cargo movement identity across the logistics domain regardless of transport mode, with DOT/PHMSA compliance for road and rail movements.
products.reference: Bill of Lading / Cargo Movement Record

attributes.name: gas_specific_gravity
attributes.description: The specific gravity of natural gas relative to air, used to characterize gas composition and quality for pipeline transportation.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14 Natural Gas Fluids Measurement

attributes.name: h2s_content_ppm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) Content Parts Per Million (PPM)
attributes.description: The concentration of hydrogen sulfide in the gas stream measured in parts per million. Critical safety and quality parameter as H2S is toxic and corrosive.
attributes.references: PHMSA Pipeline Safety Regulations 49 CFR Part 192

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this nomination record was last updated in the system, tracking the most recent change for audit and data quality purposes.

attributes.name: nominated_volume
attributes.description: The volume of crude oil or natural gas that the shipper requests to transport through the pipeline segment during the scheduling cycle.

attributes.name: nominated_volume_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the nominated volume. BOPD for crude oil (Barrels of Oil Per Day), MMCFD for natural gas (Million Cubic Feet per Day), MCFD (Thousand Cubic Feet per Day), BBL (Barrels), MCF (Thousand Cubic Feet), MMCF (Million Cubic Feet).

attributes.name: nomination_cancelled_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the nomination was cancelled by either the shipper or pipeline operator, if applicable.

attributes.name: nomination_confirmed_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the pipeline operator confirmed the nomination and communicated the scheduled volume back to the shipper.

attributes.name: nomination_cycle_type
attributes.description: The scheduling cycle period for the nomination indicating the frequency and timing window for pipeline capacity allocation.

attributes.name: nomination_effective_date
attributes.description: The gas day or operational date for which the nominated volume is scheduled to flow through the pipeline.

attributes.name: nomination_reference_number
attributes.description: External business identifier for the nomination used by shippers and pipeline operators for tracking and communication purposes.

attributes.name: nomination_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the nomination indicating its position in the pipeline scheduling workflow from submission through final confirmation or rejection.

attributes.name: nomination_submitted_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the shipper submitted the nomination to the pipeline operator for scheduling consideration.

attributes.name: operator_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes entered by the pipeline operator regarding special handling, scheduling constraints, quality issues, or other operational considerations for this nomination.

attributes.name: phmsa_pipeline_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) Pipeline Identifier (ID)
attributes.description: The PHMSA operator identification number for the pipeline system, required for regulatory reporting and safety compliance tracking.
attributes.references: PHMSA Pipeline Safety Regulations 49 CFR Part 191

attributes.name: priority_class
attributes.description: The service priority level of the nomination determining scheduling precedence. Firm service has highest priority, interruptible service is subject to curtailment, and secondary service uses available capacity.

attributes.name: proration_factor
attributes.description: The proration or allocation factor applied when pipeline capacity is oversubscribed, calculated as confirmed volume divided by nominated volume. A factor less than 1.0 indicates the nomination was cut.

attributes.name: scada_integration_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Integration Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this nomination is integrated with the SCADA pipeline monitoring system for real-time flow measurement and custody transfer validation.

attributes.name: transportation_rate
attributes.description: The tariff rate charged for transporting the product through the pipeline, typically expressed per unit volume (e.g., dollars per barrel or dollars per MCF).

attributes.name: transportation_rate_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the transportation rate, such as USD per barrel for crude oil or USD per thousand cubic feet for natural gas.

attributes.name: water_content_lbs_per_mmcf
attributes.business_glossary_term: Water Content Pounds (LBS) per Million Cubic Feet (MMCF)
attributes.description: The water content in the gas stream measured in pounds per million cubic feet, critical for preventing hydrate formation and pipeline corrosion.
attributes.references: API MPMS Chapter 14 Natural Gas Fluids Measurement

products.name: logistics_lifting_schedule
products.description: Master planning entity governing FPSO and terminal crude oil liftings and the consolidated marine logistics schedule for a given planning horizon. Captures lifting program reference, field or FPSO name, lifting month, planning period (monthly or quarterly), schedule version, cargo number, scheduled lifting date range (laycan), nominated volume (BBL), total planned liftings and volume for the period, equity holder or buyer, vessel assignment, berth assignment, loading port, number of vessels assigned, lifting status (planned, confirmed, completed, deferred), schedule status (draft, approved, published, revised), approval date, approved by, tolerance percentage, and associated lifting program references. Aligns with production sharing agreement (PSA) and joint operating agreement (JOA) lifting entitlements. Serves as the single operational master plan for marine logistics coordination, replacing separate shipping schedule and lifting program concepts.

attributes.description: FK to logistics.vessel

attributes.name: api_gravity
attributes.description: The API gravity of the crude oil or liquid hydrocarbon being lifted, measured in degrees API. Indicates the density and quality of the crude, affecting pricing, refining yield, and transportation requirements.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 11 - Physical Properties Data

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which this lifting schedule version was formally approved by the authorized planning or operations manager. Marks the transition from draft to approved status.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the manager, planner, or authorized person who approved this lifting schedule version. Provides accountability for schedule commitments.

attributes.name: berth_assignment
attributes.description: The specific berth, jetty, or loading terminal position assigned for this lifting operation. Identifies the physical loading point at the FPSO, offshore terminal, or onshore export facility.
attributes.references: API Recommended Practice 2350 - Overfill Protection for Marine Vapor Control Systems

attributes.name: bill_of_lading_number
attributes.description: The unique identifier for the bill of lading document issued for this cargo lifting. Serves as the legal receipt and title document for the transported hydrocarbons.

attributes.name: cargo_number
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the specific cargo or parcel of crude oil, LNG, LPG, or NGL being lifted. Used for custody transfer tracking and bill of lading reconciliation.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 17 - Marine Measurement

attributes.name: charter_party_type
attributes.description: The type of vessel charter agreement governing this lifting. Voyage charter for single-trip hire; time charter for vessel hire over a period; bareboat charter for vessel lease without crew. Determines cost allocation and operational responsibility.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this lifting schedule record was first created in the system. Provides audit trail for schedule planning lifecycle.

attributes.name: custody_transfer_method
attributes.description: The method used to measure and verify the volume of hydrocarbons transferred during the lifting operation. Metered for flow meter measurement; gauged for tank level measurement; calculated for derived volumes from multiple measurements. Determines the basis for commercial settlement and revenue allocation.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 17 - Marine Measurement

attributes.name: demurrage_rate_usd_per_day
attributes.business_glossary_term: Demurrage Rate in United States Dollars (USD) Per Day
attributes.description: The daily rate charged if the vessel is detained beyond the agreed laytime for loading or unloading operations, measured in USD per day. Represents the financial penalty for delays in cargo operations.

attributes.name: destination_port
attributes.description: Name of the destination port, refinery, or receiving terminal where the cargo will be delivered. Identifies the endpoint of the marine transportation leg.

attributes.name: freight_rate_usd_per_bbl
attributes.business_glossary_term: Freight Rate in United States Dollars (USD) Per Barrel (BBL)
attributes.description: The transportation cost per barrel for this cargo lifting, measured in USD per BBL. Represents the marine logistics cost component for moving crude oil or liquid hydrocarbons from the loading point to the destination.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this lifting schedule record was most recently updated. Tracks the currency of schedule information and supports change management.

attributes.name: laycan_end_date
attributes.description: The latest date within the laycan window when the vessel must arrive to commence loading, beyond which the charterer may cancel the lifting. Defines the closing of the scheduled lifting window.

attributes.name: laycan_start_date
attributes.description: The earliest date within the laycan (lay days canceling) window when the vessel may arrive and commence loading operations. Defines the opening of the scheduled lifting window.

attributes.name: lifting_month
attributes.description: The calendar month for which this lifting schedule is planned, in MM-YYYY format. Represents the primary planning period for cargo liftings.

attributes.name: lifting_program_reference
attributes.description: External reference number or code identifying the lifting program to which this schedule belongs. Links to broader lifting program planning documents and Production Sharing Agreement (PSA) or Joint Operating Agreement (JOA) entitlements.

attributes.name: lifting_status
attributes.description: Current operational status of this individual cargo lifting. Tracks progression from initial planning through confirmation, execution, or deferral. Planned indicates initial nomination; confirmed indicates vessel assignment and laycan agreement; completed indicates successful cargo transfer; deferred indicates postponement to a future period; cancelled indicates lifting will not occur.

attributes.name: nominated_volume_bbl
attributes.description: The volume of crude oil or liquid hydrocarbons nominated for lifting in this cargo, measured in barrels (BBL). Represents the planned cargo size based on production forecasts and entitlement calculations.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 12 - Calculation of Petroleum Quantities

attributes.name: number_of_vessels_assigned
attributes.description: The count of vessels assigned to execute liftings during this planning period. Used for fleet capacity planning and logistics resource management.

attributes.name: planning_period_type
attributes.description: The time horizon granularity for this lifting schedule: monthly for short-term operational plans, quarterly for medium-term coordination, or annual for strategic capacity planning.

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, special instructions, operational constraints, or exceptions related to this lifting schedule. Captures context not represented in structured fields.

attributes.name: schedule_status
attributes.description: Overall status of this lifting schedule version in the planning and approval workflow. Draft indicates work in progress; approved indicates management sign-off; published indicates distribution to stakeholders and operational teams; revised indicates changes after initial publication.

attributes.name: schedule_version
attributes.description: Version number of this lifting schedule. Increments with each revision to track changes over the planning cycle as nominations are confirmed, vessels are assigned, or liftings are deferred.

attributes.name: tolerance_percentage
attributes.description: The allowable percentage variance (plus or minus) from the nominated volume that is acceptable for this lifting. Reflects contractual flexibility in cargo size due to production variability, vessel capacity constraints, or custody transfer measurement tolerances.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 17 - Marine Measurement

attributes.name: total_planned_liftings
attributes.description: The total number of individual cargo liftings planned for the period covered by this schedule. Used for capacity planning and logistics resource allocation.

attributes.name: total_planned_volume_bbl
attributes.description: The aggregate volume of all planned liftings for the period, measured in barrels (BBL). Represents the total crude oil or liquid hydrocarbon volume to be lifted across all cargoes in the schedule.
attributes.references: API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards Chapter 12 - Calculation of Petroleum Quantities

products.name: custody_transfer
products.description: Transactional record capturing the official transfer of title and custody of petroleum products between parties at a defined measurement point, including independent inspection verification and cargo inspection details. Records transfer reference, transfer date/time, measurement point ID, transferor and transferee parties, product type and grade, gross observed volume (GOV), gross standard volume (GSV), net standard volume (NSV), API gravity, BS&W percentage, sulfur content, temperature, pressure, meter ticket number, seal numbers and verification, independent inspector details (company, inspector name, inspection type — quantity/quality/draft survey/ullage survey, certificate number), draft survey results, inspection date, inspection port (load or discharge), and transfer status. Critical for revenue recognition, JIB, quality claims, royalty calculations, and custody transfer dispute resolution.
products.reference: API MPMS Custody Transfer / Meter Ticket

attributes.name: api_gravity
attributes.description: Measure of petroleum liquid density relative to water, expressed in API degrees, used for volume correction and product valuation.

attributes.name: bsw_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of non-hydrocarbon impurities (sediment and water) in the product, deducted from gross volume to calculate net volume for custody transfer.
